title: jnprofile-rust
text: jnprofile-rust is the Rust profile of jnterfaces. A profile sets up a project in one language. It has tools, for example lint, and each tool brings its recipes. A recipe is a command of the project’s Justfile, such as just lint. The profile is for a Rust project with Cargo. The installer finds such a project by its Cargo.toml. The profile gives the project the real steps of the commit gates. A step is one recipe that just check runs, and it fails when the change breaks a rule.

title: jnprofile-rust
text: jnterfaces has the rust profile since jnterfaces#34, and installs its programs since jnterfaces#39. The jnterfaces entry keeps the entry and the change to the installer that it took. Run this command in a project that has the jnterfaces installer: just install --profile rust In a folder with no Cargo.toml, the command first runs cargo init --vcs none. It then installs the six tools lint, typecheck, test, integration, docstring and api. If you do not choose other roles, it also turns on the default roles of the profile, tasker and prose. The section The roles of the jnterfaces guide says what each role installs. The machine needs Rust from rustup, and the programs that jnterfaces needs. The profile installs the rest with rustup and cargo. The key programs of profile.json names each program, how the installer checks it, and how it installs it. The installer checks the programs of each tool that it installs, in the project folder. It runs cargo +stable install in the home folder, so the stable toolchain builds the programs, whatever the project pins, and also when rustup has no default toolchain. The profile installs stable with the minimal profile when it is missing. The checks run in the project folder, so rustup reads the rust-toolchain.toml of the project, and a component goes to the toolchain that the project pins. Program Use Install rustup 1.28.0 or later Every step https://rustup.rs/. The installer stops if it is missing or older. An older rustup installs a missing pinned toolchain during a check The toolchain, with cargo Every step The profile runs rustup toolchain install when the toolchain that rust-toolchain.toml or rust-toolchain pins is missing. With no pin and no default toolchain, run rustup default stable yourself rustfmt and clippy fmt, fmt-check, lint and docstring-check The profile runs rustup component add llvm-tools-preview and cargo-llvm-cov The coverage of test, integration and coverage-check The profile runs rustup component add llvm-tools-preview and cargo +stable install --locked cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1. Version 0.9.1 or later passes the check The nightly toolchain nightly-2026-11-12 api-check, through smalldocs and rustdoc The profile runs rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-11-12 --profile minimal in the home folder. It does not change the default toolchain taplo and cargo-sort The tool toml, if you install it The profile runs cargo +stable install --locked taplo-cli@0.10.0 and cargo +stable install --locked cargo-sort@2.1.4. These versions or later pass the check just Every recipe cargo install just uv diff-cover and the helper script of the steps https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ jlog v0.3.0 just install of jnterfaces, which runs each step through it Run the command under this table, then put ~/.local/bin on PATH. It downloads the release binary and checks its SHA-256. To build it from source, clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jlog, run git checkout v0.3.0, then just install there This command installs the release binary of jlog: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rahuldave/jlog/v0.3.0/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --tag v0.3.0

text: Before jnterfaces#34, the installer of jnterfaces stopped with “The profile.json of the rust profile is malformed” for two reasons: The manifest. check_profile accepts only pyproject.toml and package.json as the key manifest. The rust profile names Cargo.toml. A tool with no packages. check_profile needs at least one package for each tool. The tools of the rust profile are programs of the machine, so each tool has the empty list []. A third change follows from the first. present_packages reads the packages that the project file already has. It reads Cargo.toml as JSON, fails, and then the installer says “cannot read Cargo.toml”. The change reads the table [dev-dependencies], where cargo add --dev puts a crate. title: The jnterfaces entry
section: What jnterfaces reads from the profile
text: The key code of profile.json holds the @code globs, here **/*.rs. The gate reads them for the required targets. The user approved the name code. The spec has the installer copy the globs into the key code of .agents/stack.json, for each profile. jnterfaces#34 added that to the installer. The Python and TypeScript profiles need the same key. The key programs of profile.json lists each program that the profile needs, with the command that checks it and, for most, the command that installs it. A tool names its programs under programs, and so does the base. The installer of jnterfaces reads the key since jnterfaces#39. The commands are split with shlex.split and run with no shell. A program with no install command, here only rustup, is checked before the installer writes anything, and stops it with its description. The others are checked in the project folder after the files are written, installed when the check fails, and checked again. A program can have a version floor in version, such as >=0.10.0, which the installer reads since jnterfaces#57. The check passes when the first version in its output is the floor or later. The profile gives a floor to rustup, cargo-llvm-cov, taplo, cargo-sort and the nightly. A cargo +stable install line installs the floor itself. A newer version passes too, so the profile pins no minor line. An install runs in the folder that install_in names, project by default or home. The cargo +stable install lines run in home, after the program stable makes sure that rustup has the stable toolchain. So they build with stable, whatever the project pins, and also when rustup has no default toolchain. The program after rustup is toolchain. Its check is rustup show active-toolchain. When the rust-toolchain.toml or rust-toolchain file of the project pins a toolchain that rustup does not have, rustup 1.29.3 would install it during the check. The installer runs each check with RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 since jnterfaces#57, so the check fails, and then rustup toolchain install installs the pinned toolchain. A rustup older than 1.28.0 installs the toolchain during rustup --version whatever the variable says, so the floor of rustup is >=1.28.0. cargo is not a program of its own, because cargo --version fails in that case too. A machine where rustup has no default toolchain, as after rustup-init --default-toolchain none, fails the check in a project with no pin. rustup toolchain install with no name fails there too. So in a project that has a Cargo.toml, the installer stops and prints the description of toolchain, which says to run rustup default stable or to pin a toolchain. In a folder with no Cargo.toml, cargo init fails first, before the installer checks the programs, and rustup prints its own hint. The profile does not run rustup default stable itself, because that would change the default of rustup on each machine that has none, also for a project that pins its toolchain. The key tests of profile.json holds the globs of the test files, here tests/**, the folder tests at the top of the project. A wider glob such as **/tests/** would also take a module in src/ and bring its new code into the parent. The installer copies the globs into the key tests of .agents/stack.json, for each profile; jnterfaces#46 added that. test-parent of agent_gest_git_skills reads that key, and copies only those files into the worktree of the parent. The step names are the recipe names. The profile gives fmt-check, lint, typecheck, test, integration, coverage-check and docstring-check, and also test-paths for the test-parent recipe. The key verify of each tool lists the steps of the tool, so just rust verify runs all seven steps today. The folder .agents/targets/rust/ is an extra of skill-package.json, so the installer copies it as it copies .agents/just/rust/.

title: The jnterfaces entry
section: What the profile needs from jnterfaces
text: The module sets working-directory. The installer writes set working-directory := '../..' into each module, so that the recipes run at the top of the project. The spec allows that setting in a module, and it forbids only a [working-directory] attribute on a recipe. The recipes of this profile need the setting. A module does not take the shell of the root Justfile. With just 1.50, a set shell in the root Justfile reaches the recipes of the root and of its imports, but not the recipes of a mod. The recipes of the profile are in the module rust.just, so the installer writes set shell into that file, as the spec says. The lab checks that the line is there, and runs the recipes with a stand-in jlog. The run ID. The index runs just --justfile ... rust test and just --justfile ... rust coverage-check as two calls of just, so a dependency of coverage-check on test would run the tests twice. The spec now gives each run of just one run ID. The root Justfile has the line export JLOG_RUN := env("JLOG_RUN", uuid()), and no module may have it. test saves the run ID and the worktree tree next to its report, and coverage-check reads the report only when both match. Otherwise it runs the tests itself. The installer writes the line into the root Justfile, and the lab checks it. Without the line, coverage-check runs the tests each time, and just rust verify runs them twice.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The rules for a commit live in the global CLAUDE.md file and in AGENTS.md files. They say that a commit needs lint, tests, integration tests, types and docs checks, and an adversarial review. They also say that the docs of a public repository go to a website. Nothing checks these rules. An agent can commit without a review. No record shows what ran. The parts of a solution exist, but they are not joined: The just command contract of jnterfaces names the recipes fmt, lint, typecheck, test, integration and verify. It says not to add a recipe that does nothing, so the set of recipes changes from repository to repository. The grv skill tells an agent to do an adversarial review. No check makes sure that the review happened. The Claude hooks of agent_gest_git_skills add the commit docs when an agent commits. The Codex hooks have no commit hook. GitButler is in the hooks, skills and docs of agent_gest_git_skills, mostly for stacked PRs. The spec drops it. The Python profile installs the pre-commit framework, which owns .git/hooks/pre-commit and changes files at commit time. The spec moves the framework to the tasker role. jagt renders and checks task packets for agents. No recipe uses it for a review.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: Term Meaning Gate A check that stops a commit when it fails. Lab A test that runs a real scenario in a temporary repository and checks the result. Role A package of skills that the jnterfaces installer adds to a project, for example tasker. Tasker The role of agent_gest_git_skills. It adds the Gest skills, the hooks and the worktree recipes. Profile The tools of one language, for example jnprofile-python. Owner A part of the stack that adds lines or parts to a shared file: jnterfaces, a profile, a tool of a profile, or a role. Worktree tree The tree hash of all the files in the worktree, staged or not. The section “The worktree tree” says how to compute it. Commit tree The tree hash of the index at commit time. Log folder The folder .agents/log/ of a worktree. Git ignores it. Shared log folder The log folder of the main checkout. All worktrees of a repository write their packets and records there. Run log The file .agents/log/just.jsonl of a worktree, with one JSON line for each event. Step One recipe that just check runs, for example lint. No-op step A step with no tool in the repository. It logs a skip and does no work. Pass A line in the run log that says every step passed for one worktree tree. Agentic target A recipe that writes a jagt task packet for an agent. It does no work itself, other than logged steps that give the agent its inputs, such as test-parent. Fresh agent An agent that a harness starts for one task, for example a subagent. Record The saved result of an agentic target, with its input tree and its output tree. Harness A program that runs an agent, for example Claude Code or Codex. Plugin A small Python script for one harness. It knows where that harness keeps its sessions and transcripts. Adapter The parts that join one harness to the gates: its hooks in agent_gest_git_skills, and its plugin in the repository of jlog. Agent hook A hook of a harness that runs before or after a tool call. smalldocs The program that builds the docs websites of the stack. Docments The comments beside the arguments of a Python function. smalldocs reads them for the API pages. API pages The pages of a docs website that smalldocs makes from the code of a package. smalldocs 0.5.5 makes them for Python only.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The gates stop honest mistakes, for example an agent that forgets the review, or a commit with an unstaged fix. They do not stop an agent that tries to cheat. An agent with a shell can edit the log, remove the git hook or write a commit with git commit-tree. The spec makes these acts hard to do by accident. A commit that skips the gate has no trailer of the gate, so just ci stops it in CI.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: Every repository has the same steps, for any language: just check fmt-check lint typecheck test integration coverage-check docstring-check docs-check prose-check diff-check jnterfaces names the steps. It holds the list and the meaning of each step. The installer writes a no-op step for each name that no installed profile and no installed role file defines: typecheck: jlog skip typecheck "no type checker in this repository" The profiles and roles fill in the steps. jnprofile-python, jnprofile-typescript and jnprofile-rust replace the no-op steps with real commands. Most of the commands of a language come from the profile. A role file can fill a step too, as nossaifd fills prose-check. A repository can replace a step of a profile, or a no-op step, with a recipe of the same name in its own Justfile. How the installer knows. It reads recipe names with just --dump. The root Justfile imports the index, so a dump of the root would also hold the old index. So the installer reads the names in this order: It keeps a copy of the old index. Then it writes the index in its form with the modules only. That form has the mod lines, with no role file, no combined recipe and no no-op step. It dumps the root Justfile. Those names are the names of the repository. The recipes of a module have the name of the module in front, so they never meet a step name. If this dump fails, the installer stops with the error of just. It never goes on as if the repository had no recipe. It dumps each role file alone, and each module alone, as now. It writes the whole index. It leaves out each combined recipe and each no-op step whose name the repository defines. It writes a no-op step only for a step name that no role file and no combined recipe has. When it stops before the end of step 4, it puts the old index back. So just check keeps the steps that it had. A role step and a repository recipe of one name. The index imports the role file, so both define the name. Then just would stop with “Recipe redefined”. The installer stops first, and it names the recipe and the role. Without this rule, just stops with “Recipe redefined”. With set allow-duplicate-recipes, the recipe nearer the root wins. So the no-op step of the index would beat the role file that the index imports. A skip counts only for a step that no profile and no role provides. If an installed profile or role provides a step, a skip of that step is a failure. So a broken index of recipes cannot pass by skipping everything. agent_gest_git_skills tests that the steps exist. The gate reads just --summary, which runs no backticks. If a step or a required target is missing, the gate stops the commit and says “run just install”. It holds no command of a language. Steps only check. A step never changes a tracked file, or a file that git does not ignore. fmt-check checks the format, and fmt stays outside just check. Caches and reports, such as target/, .coverage and lcov.info, go to ignored paths. Each profile adds those paths to .gitignore through the shared-file writer. coverage-check fails when a changed line of code does not run in the tests. The report. test and integration write their coverage as LCOV or Cobertura files in ignored paths. Python uses pytest-cov, TypeScript uses c8 and Rust uses cargo llvm-cov. The check. The step runs diff-cover on the reports of both against the parent commit, with --fail-under 100. A line that only integration runs counts when integration is in just check. When the setup answer puts integration only in just verify, such a line needs a pragma or an exclude, or the person moves integration back into just check. No old report. The index of jnterfaces calls just once for each language and step, so a dependency of one module recipe cannot keep the tests from running twice. A run ID does. Where the ID comes from. The root Justfile has the line export JLOG_RUN := env("JLOG_RUN", uuid()). The first just call makes the ID, and each just call inside it inherits it. A module gets the ID of the root. A module must not have the line, because env() reads the process environment, so the module would make a second ID. The ID is bound to a tree. A person can set JLOG_RUN by hand. So jlog writes the worktree tree with the first line of a run. jlog pass and coverage-check reject a run whose first tree is not the current worktree tree. An old run of the same tree is a valid run. Who uses it. jlog writes JLOG_RUN as the run ID of each line, so the steps of one just check share one run, even in inner just calls. jlog pass reads the lines of that run. test and integration write it into their reports. coverage-check reads a report only when its run ID matches. Otherwise it runs the tests itself. Lines left out. In Python and TypeScript, a line can be left out with the pragma of its tool, # pragma: no cover or /* c8 ignore next */. Stable Rust has no pragma for a line, so the Rust profile reads an exclude list of files, .agents/coverage-exclude.txt, instead. The test-review target must accept each new pragma and each new entry in the list. Generated code. The paths in .agents/generated.txt count for neither coverage-check nor docstring-check. Each profile passes them to its tools as excludes. The lists come from the parent. The steps read generated.txt and coverage-exclude.txt with git show HEAD: , so a commit cannot exempt its own code. With no parent, or when the parent has no such file, git show fails and the list is empty. test-review judges each new entry. No tests. When code changed and there is no report, the step fails and says “write tests”. When no profile provides test, the step is a skip. The first commit. With no parent, diff-cover cannot run. The step runs the report tool of the profile over all code with a limit of 100%, for example coverage report --fail-under=100, c8 check-coverage --lines 100 or cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 100. docstring-check fails when a class, function or method has no doc, and in Python and Rust also a module. It covers private items too. Only the public items go on the API pages. Python: interrogate with --fail-under 100. The docments of public functions are checked once, by smalldocs api check in docs-check. TypeScript: eslint with only the rule jsdoc/require-jsdoc of eslint-plugin-jsdoc, set for all classes, methods, functions and arrow functions, exported or not. Biome has no rule for a missing JSDoc comment, so the profile adds eslint for this one step. Rust: cargo clippy with -W missing_docs and -W clippy::missing_docs_in_private_items, with --cap-lints warn. The step reads the JSON messages of clippy, and fails on each item with no doc outside generated.txt. It does not use -D, for two reasons. -D fails on a generated file too. It also stops clippy before it checks the binaries that use a failing library. A suppression in the code, such as #[allow(missing_docs)] in Rust, beats the command line. The docs lens of review gives a finding for each new one that has no reason. Its output lists each item with no doc, with its file and line. The author agent writes the docs from this list. No target writes them. diff-check runs git diff --cached --check HEAD, so it checks the changes of the commit for whitespace errors. A lint finds steps that the run log cannot see. It finds these: A shebang line or the [script] attribute. Such a recipe does not run through jlog. The test and typecheck recipes of both profiles have shebang lines now, so the profiles change. A line with a - prefix, which ignores a failure. [no-cd], or a [working-directory] attribute on a recipe. Each changes the folder in which jlog looks for the log folder. The setting set working-directory that the installer writes into a module, to the top of the project, is allowed. prose-check checks the changed pages with the checker of nossaifd. The pages. A page is a file that is_page of nossaifd’s prose_gate.py accepts, so prose-check and the turn gate use one rule. It takes .md and .qmd files, and it skips files such as AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the folder .agents/. The changed pages on a machine. prose_gate.py check-changed finds them: the pages that git diff --no-renames --diff-filter=AMT HEAD names, and the untracked pages. T is a changed type, such as a link that became a file. With no commit yet, it compares with the empty tree, so each page of the index counts. The changed pages in CI. A CI checkout has no change against HEAD, so that list is empty. In CI, check-changed checks the pages that changed between BASE and HEAD, and also the pages that changed against HEAD. In a clean checkout the second set is empty. On a machine where a tool sets CI, the second set still holds the pages of the next commit. The option --base REF does the same outside CI, and it wins over CI. CI is on when the variable CI is set to a value other than empty, 0 and false. Where BASE comes from. It is always a merge base, so the check never takes in the pages of commits that only the other side has. On a pull request, BASE is the merge base of origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF and HEAD. On a push to the default branch, BASE is the commit before the push. It is the key before of the file at $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH. So a direct push of several commits gets each of them checked, also when a person skipped the gate with --no-verify. When before is all zeros, the push made the branch, as the first push of a new repository does. Then the step compares with the empty tree, so each page is checked. When before is not in the history, or is not an ancestor of HEAD, BASE is HEAD^. On another push, a merge queue, or another CI system, BASE is the merge base of HEAD and the default branch. So a branch with several commits gets each of them checked, also after a force-push. When that merge base is HEAD itself, as in a build of the default branch, BASE is HEAD^. The default branch comes from the key repository.default_branch of the file at $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, or else from origin/HEAD. When neither gives a branch, the step exits with 2. On the first push, with no parent, the step compares the empty tree with HEAD, with a diff of two arguments. A diff with ... needs a commit on each side, so it cannot take the empty tree. The event pull_request_target checks out the base branch, so the diff would be empty. The step exits with 2 and names the event pull_request. Full history in CI. The CI job checks out with fetch-depth: 0. The step asks git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository. In a shallow clone, it exits with 2 and names fetch-depth: 0. So a cut-off history never counts as a first push. No changed page. The step passes. check alone exits with 2 when it gets no page, so the step never calls it with an empty list. The checker. check-changed checks the pages as prose_gate.py check PAGE... does. The step never calls check.py directly. check applies the map of checkers in .agents/nossaifd-checkers.json, so a talk repository can check its slides with another checker. It names the checker in its output. A checker that is missing or that fails is a hard problem. Any exit of check-changed other than 0 fails the step. One line. A step has no shebang line. So the logic goes into prose_gate.py, and the recipe calls it once. The recipe is in the role file of nossaifd, .agents/just/roles/nossaifd.just, with the name prose-check. So it fills the step in a project with the nossaifd role. Without the role, the step is a no-op step. The API pages. The step runs smalldocs api module NAME for each changed module into a temporary file, and checks that file. No writes. The step writes nothing into the repository. When prose_gate.py or its checker is missing, the step fails and prints the install line. The integration answer of the setup questions decides whether integration is in the list. The list is in .agents/stack.json. jlog pass and the gate read the list from there. The contract changes. The rule “Do not add recipes that do nothing” becomes “A step with no tool is a no-op step that logs the skip.”

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
section: The docs site and the API pages
text: Today no profile gives a new project a docs site. The recipes docs-check and docs-publish exist only in the Justfiles of jnterfaces, the profile repositories and agent_gest_git_skills, for their own websites. A docs tool in jnterfaces, for any language. It writes the smalldocs config and docs/index.md. It fills docs-check with smalldocs check docs. It adds docs-publish and a CI workflow that runs it. The name docs-publish matches the recipes that exist now. An api tool in jnprofile-python. It adds the api settings to the smalldocs config. The key packages names the packages of the project. The tool adds smalldocs api check to docs-check. That command exits with 1 when it finds a gap, as the code of smalldocs 0.5.5 shows. The step runs it with uv run --with smalldocs==0.5.5, so the package and its dependencies can be imported. The profile turns the tool on by default when the project has the docs tool. No API pages for TypeScript or Rust yet. smalldocs 0.5.5 reads the API with the Python ast module and reads the docments with fastcore. Work is under way in smalldocs to read the API of Rust with rustdoc and of TypeScript with JSDoc. Until a release has it, a TypeScript or Rust project gets the docs tool only. After that release, jnprofile-typescript adds an api tool like the one of Python. That tool pins the new release, and it says which source files @api names. jnprofile-rust adds its api tool after the release that reads rustdoc.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The skills ask for the work, and the steps and targets check it. The skills ask the author agent to write tests and docs. gim, gte and gdo say that each change needs tests and a doc for each item. The author agent has the context of the change, so it writes them. No jagt target writes tests or docstrings. The steps check that they exist. test, coverage-check and docstring-check are deterministic and logged. The agentic targets check that they are good. test-review checks the tests, and the docs lens of review checks the docstrings. A part of a skill becomes a target only when the gate needs its evidence. The other parts of the skills stay as they are. The doc pages are the exception. just update-docs writes the pages that a change affects, such as the README and the guides. A fresh agent can do that work, because it needs the whole change and not the context of one function.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The g* skills keep the craft, and lose the commands of each language. Each check that a skill runs goes through a recipe, so the run log has it. Skill The change gim It writes the code, the tests and the docs. It ends with just check and the required targets, and it fixes what their findings say. It runs no checks of its own. gte It says how to write a good test. It runs tests only through just test, just integration and just coverage-check. It holds the base tasks of test-review and visual-check. gfm It runs just fmt, then the check steps. It names no tool such as ruff or biome, because the profiles own the tools. gdo It asks the author for a doc on every item, and it reads the output of docstring-check. It holds the base tasks of update-docs and visualize. grv It holds the base task of review, with the lenses and the docs lens. To run grv by hand is to run just review. gcm It commits after the pass and the records. It explains a stop of the gate, asks the person before record-skip, and uses stacked PRs with plain git. gpa, gor They use stacks with plain git, the shared log folder, and records from worktrees. gsu It runs just install, with the setup questions and the check of the tools. gtw, gbs, gsp, gpl, gis, gpr No change. Their work gives no evidence that the gate needs. When a repository has no just check, each skill tells the agent to run gsu first.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: An agentic target adds a skill to the work at the moment that the work needs it. The skill has typed inputs and a fixed form of result, a little like a module of DSPy without a signature. The arguments of a just recipe are the inputs. A later spec can add signatures, with a type for each argument and each field of the result. The targets work with any harness. They depend only on these parts: jagt render writes an AGENT_TASK v1 packet. It is plain text, so any harness can read it. The rules of the jagt-protocol skill. The agent that reads a packet gives the task to a fresh agent, and does not do it itself. The fresh agent returns an AGENT_RESULT v1 packet as its last message. The skill is optional in jnterfaces now. It becomes required when the gates are installed. An adapter for each harness says how the result becomes a record. The section “Records” lists the adapters. Each packet has these parts: The base task from the skill. For example, grv gives the review lenses. A lens is one point of view of the review, for example correctness, tests or safety. The file is references/targets/ .md in the skill. The recipe looks for that file in each installed skill, and one skill must have it. So the nossaifd skill gives the base task of prose, and a target without its skill prints no packet. The language layer from .agents/targets/ / .md, for each language in .agents/stack.json. Each profile ships its files, as it ships its just modules now. For example, the Python file for update-docs can say “write docments for each argument”. A new language needs a new file, and no change to any skill. The repository text from .agents/targets/ .md, if the file exists. For example, .agents/targets/review.md can say “check each SQL migration for a rollback”. The inputs: the diff, the input tree and the arguments of the recipe. The diff compares the worktree with HEAD, and holds the files that git does not track yet. It is the file diffs/ - .diff in the shared log folder, so the same tree on another HEAD gets a file of its own. Before the recipe computes the tree, it makes .agents/log/.gitignore with the line * if the file is missing. So the run log of jlog and the diff file are not in the tree. The recipe stops if .agents, .agents/log, its diffs folder or this file is a link. It opens each folder through the folder above it, so a link that appears later moves nothing. It writes each diff as a new file, so a link or a hard link at its name keeps the other file. In the main checkout, it also stops if .git is a link to a folder elsewhere. So it writes nothing outside the repository. From a linked worktree, the main checkout is the folder that holds the real .git, as git names it, even when the .git of the main checkout is a link. The allowed actions: what the fresh agent may do. A target that changes files names them, such as “change the docs that the change affects”. The required outputs: the fields that the result must have, for example findings and status. A nonce: a random value of 32 lowercase hex digits, whose first digit is a letter. It is the one random part of a packet. The rest of the packet text is the same for the same inputs. jagt render saves the version of the file form, the nonce, the target, the input tree, the path of the worktree and the hash of the packet in packets/ .json in the shared log folder. In the packet and the result, the nonce is a top-level field, nonce:. The fresh agent copies it from the packet into its AGENT_RESULT v1. The check. Before the hook or just record writes a record, it runs jagt result lint --expect-target   --expect-nonce  . A result with another nonce, with none, or with two nonce fields gives no record. Without a record. jagt render --no-save gives the text only, with no nonce and no file, for demos and labs. The first agentic targets: Target What the fresh agent does Its result just review An adversarial review of the changes, on the strongest model. The docs lens checks that each new or changed doc says what the item is for, that it matches the code, and that it is not a stub. Findings, each one fixed with a test or with a reason not to fix it. just test-review Checks that each new behavior has a test, that each new test checks a result, and that each new pragma or exclude has a reason. A new test that passed on the parent commit is a finding, unless the change is a refactor. Findings, each one fixed with a test or with a reason not to fix it. just update-docs [area] Finds the docs that the change affects, and writes or changes them. The repository text says which docs the repository has, for example user docs, developer docs, API docs or a change log. The changed docs, and the docs it checked and left alone. just prose [path] Applies the nossaifd guide to the changed pages and docstrings, beyond check.py: the plain-writing pass and the pass that removes the habits of model writing. The changed pages, and the lint output after the change. just visual-check [url-or-flow] Runs the app, goes through the flow in a browser and takes screenshots. The screenshots, shown to the person, and a pass or fail for each step of the flow. just visualize [topic] Draws a diagram of a part of the code, for a doc or for the person. The diagram file and the doc that shows it. Before it writes its packet, the test-review recipe runs the recipe test-parent, through .agents/skills/gcm/scripts/test_parent.py: It makes a worktree of the parent commit in a temporary folder outside the repository, with git worktree add --detach. It copies each added or changed test file in, runs the recipe  ::test-paths of the parent on each file alone, and removes the worktree. A file that does not build cannot hide a file that passes. A parent with no such recipe gives “the runner failed”. Test files. Each profile names its test files with the globs of the key tests of profile.json. test-parent copies only those files, so no new code reaches the parent. A Rust unit test lives in the file of its code. Copying that file copies the new code too, so a pass proves nothing. So the key tests of the Rust profile names tests/** only, and test-review judges the unit tests from the diff alone. Two limits of the Rust profile. The tests of a workspace member, such as crates/x/tests/a.rs, do not match tests/**. The glob **/tests/** would also take src/x/tests/mod.rs, which can bring new code into the parent. So test-review judges the tests of a member from the diff. A build script of a dependency can fail for an outside reason, such as a missing system library. cargo prints the same lines as for a test that does not build, so test-paths exits with 1, not 2. The exit codes of test-paths. Each profile gives the same four: 0: the tests ran and passed. 1: a test failed, or a test did not build. A new test of new code often does not build on the parent, and that is a failure of the test. 5: no test ran, as pytest exits when it collects no test. An example is a file whose tests are all skipped. An xfail test, which is expected to fail, does not count as a test that ran. test-paths with no path exits with 5 too, and it never runs all the tests. Any other code: the runner itself failed, for example with a usage error, a crash, or an install of the environment that fails. A test that ends the run, as with os._exit(0), gives this code too. One line for each test. The output of test-paths names each test and its result. In a file with a test that fails, a test that passes gives no case of its own, so test-review reads those lines. Each profile counts the tests. It reads the count from a report or the output of the runner, such as the JUnit report of pytest or the lines “running N tests” of cargo. A plugin can change the terminal output of pytest, so the Python profile reads the report. A count of 0 gives 5, even when the runner exits with 0. A runner that exits with 5 for another reason, such as a fatal error of Node, gets 2. vitest exits with 1 when a test fails, and also when it finds no test file. So the profile reads its output to tell the two apart. No test file. When no changed file matches tests, as in a change with Rust unit tests only, test-parent does not call test-paths. It records “no test ran on the parent”. How test-parent reads them. 0 is a pass on the parent. 1 is the expected failure. 5 is “no test ran on the parent”, and test-review judges those tests from the diff. Any other code is “the runner failed”, which is neither a pass nor a failure. Two limits of the Python profile. pytest finds its config from the test files that it runs. So a pytest.ini in the folder of a test file takes the place of the config of the project, as it does when you run pytest on that file yourself. test-parent stops the process group of each run. A test that leaves its group, as with setsid, can outlive the run. It writes the result, with the output of the tests, to test-parent/ .json in the log folder.   is the worktree tree, as the gate computes it, so the packet of test-review for that tree finds it. The result names the case. It exits with 0 in each case above. It exits with 1 only when test-parent itself fails. Examples are a worktree that git cannot make, a copy that fails, and a log file that it cannot write. On SIGTERM, SIGHUP or Ctrl-C it stops the tests and removes the worktree before it exits. The packet holds the result. So the run is logged, and the agent only judges it. On the first commit, test-parent is a skip. The base task of test-review is in gte, and the base task of review is in grv. Two recipes have the name prose now, and both change: The role file of nossaifd has a recipe prose. It becomes prose-check, and it fills the step in each project with the nossaifd role. jnterfaces itself has a recipe prose checker in its own Justfile. It becomes prose-check. In jnterfaces it replaces the step, as the recipe of a repository may. When jnterfaces takes the gates for itself, the recipe must run with no argument, as each step does. So prose is free for the agentic target. The target that writes docs is update-docs, not docs. Many repositories have a recipe docs that previews the docs site, as the docs tool does. A role file that also had docs would stop each Justfile that imports it, because just refuses a recipe that two files define. Other targets to consider later: just security-review: looks for secrets, injection and unsafe input. just impact [symbol]: finds the code that depends on a changed symbol, with ast-grep. just pr-text: writes the PR description from the commits and records. just ci-triage [run]: reads a failed CI run and finds the cause.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: Some choices of a repository belong to the person, not to the stack. Today the installer asks yes-or-no questions at a terminal, and only about new roles. With no terminal and no saved choices, it stops. The spec makes these changes: At a terminal, the installer asks the open questions itself. A question can have more than two answers. With no terminal, under an agent, the installer writes a packet with the open questions, and stops. The packet is a just setup-questions packet. The agent that ran the installer asks the person, with the question tool of its harness. It does not give this packet to a fresh agent, because a fresh agent cannot ask the person. Then it runs just install --answer  =  for each answer. In CI, when CI is set, the installer takes the defaults and asks nothing. A question with an answer in .agents/stack.json is not asked again. A later version of the stack can add questions, and then only the new ones are asked. The first questions: Key Question Default issues Which Gest tasks become GitHub issues: every top-level task, only development tasks, or none? Every top-level task docs-publish Publish the docs site of a public repository after a merge to main? Yes integration Run the integration tests in just check, or only in just verify before a PR? In just check tasker One branch in the main checkout, or a worktree for each task? The answer sets the variant of the tasker role, git or gitwt. git review-model Which model does the adversarial review? The strongest model of the harness The required targets are not a question. .agents/targets/required.txt is the only place for them.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: A record has two trees. The input tree is the worktree tree when the packet was made. The output tree is the worktree tree when the fresh agent stopped, after its changes. A target that changes no file has the same tree twice. The chain. update-docs and prose change files, so the gate accepts a chain: update-docs T0 -> T1 prose T1 -> T2 test-review T2 -> T2 review T2 -> T2 check T2 Each record must start at the output tree of the record before it. The last tree must be the commit tree. An update-docs record comes before a prose record, because prose checks the text that update-docs wrote. test-review and review come after the last record that changes files. When a review leads to fixes, the fixes make a new tree, and the review runs again on it. test-review and review change no files, so they can run in either order on the same tree. What a record must hold. A record counts only if its status is success, and each finding is fixed with a test or has a reason not to fix it. The turn gate of nossaifd stays, with a different job. nossaifd has its own hooks, UserPromptSubmit and Stop, in Claude Code and Codex. At the end of a turn, the Stop hook blocks once when a page that the turn changed has a hard problem or no recorded pass. The jobs. The turn gate asks early, inside a turn, at little cost. The commit gate decides. Only the prose record and the prose-check step let a commit through. One store of page passes. nossaifd records the pass of a page with prose_gate.py record, in nossaifd/ under git rev-parse --git-common-dir. Every worktree shares it. The store stays there, with or without the gates, so it needs no migration. The prose target records each page. The fresh agent of just prose runs prose_gate.py record for each page that it passed. So a page that just prose passed does not block a later turn. A page pass is not a prose record. The gate needs the prose record of the tree, from the fresh agent. When the gates are installed, .agents/stack.json lists the tasker role. Then the message of the Stop block says “run just prose”. The steps by hand alone give a page pass, but no prose record. The records are in the shared log folder, in records/. A fresh agent can work in another worktree, for example in the parallel work of the gor skill. The packet holds the path of its worktree, so the hook computes the tree in the right checkout. The gate reads only records. It does not know which harness made them. The file of a record is a JSON file in records/, with these keys: Key What it holds version 1. target The name of the target, for example review. status The status of the result. Only success counts. input_tree, output_tree The two trees of the record. findings A list. Each finding has a summary, and a test that shows the fix or a reason not to fix it. source hook, agent for just record, or skip for just record-skip. reason For a skip, the reason. A skip has the same tree twice. model, nonce The model of the fresh agent, and the nonce of its packet. The gate is .agents/skills/gcm/scripts/commit_gate.py. Who writes a record depends on the adapter of the harness: Harness How the result becomes a record Claude Code The SubagentStop hook gets the last message of the fresh agent and the path of its transcript. It finds the nonce in the message. The packet file gives the target, the input tree and the worktree. The plugin reads the model from the transcript. Codex The same as Claude Code. Codex 0.163 has the hooks SubagentStart and SubagentStop, with agent_transcript_path and last_assistant_message. Codex runs the hooks of a project only after the person trusts them. An older Codex, or any other harness The agent that ran the target runs just record    , and the record is marked "source": "agent". In Claude Code, just record stops, because the hook writes the records. The script cannot tell whether a Codex has the hook, so in Codex just record checks the result instead. An agent can clear the variables of its harness, so they cannot say that no harness runs. A repository with the record hook. There, just record without CODEX_THREAD_ID stops. The hook can be in .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .codex/hooks.json or .codex/config.toml. The script reads them in the checkout where it runs and in the main checkout, and the guard protects both. It also reads the settings of the person in ~/.claude and ~/.codex. The check of a just record in Codex reads the transcript of the fresh agent, a JSONL file in the sessions folder of CODEX_HOME, by default ~/.codex/sessions. The record takes the result from the transcript, not from the file of the agent: A forked agent is not a fresh agent. Its transcript holds the turns of its parent, so the check refuses a transcript with forked_from_id or with more than one session_meta line. Its session_meta line names the parent thread in parent_thread_id. The parent must be the thread that ran just record, from CODEX_THREAD_ID. One fresh agent can have several turns. The nonce must be in the last_agent_message of one of its task_complete lines. The model comes from the turn context of the transcript. The check reads no SQLite file. A reader of a database in WAL mode writes to its -shm file, so a read is not free of writes. A read of ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite on 2026-11-12 changed the time of state_5.sqlite-shm. A skip with a reason. just record-skip     lets one tree through without that record. The agent hooks ask the person before it runs. Codex has no question for a hook, so there the hook stops the command, and the agent asks the person to run it. One result, one record. The record of a packet is records/ .json, and a second result of the same packet gives no record. The findings must be a list in outputs.findings, or the result gives no record. The guard of the records. The gate guard stops these calls: record_result.py hook, which only the harness runs. just record in Claude Code. The guard finds the recipe after the options of just, and it reads the options from just --help. A record command that sets or unsets CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_THREAD_ID or CODEX_HOME, or that runs with env, exec, unset or export -n. Those programs can clear the variables without their names. A write to the sessions folder of Codex. A write to .git/config, where a core.hooksPath would move the hooks. A commit while git has a core.hooksPath. The guard asks git once, in the folder of the command. Then git would not run the gate. Any git line when the guard itself fails. A line without git runs. The limits of the records. The guard reads the words of a line. It does not run the shell in its head, so a command that hides git runs: A program such as python -c, or a script, can commit or write a file in records/. A here-doc or a pipe into a shell, as in bash <<EOF, runs. So does a word that the shell makes, as in git $(echo commit) -n. A setting that a command writes first, as in ~/.gitconfig, can give git a core.hooksPath that the guard does not see. A record hook in a setting that the script does not read, such as the managed settings or a plugin of Codex, does not stop just record. In a repository with no record hook, just record takes the result from the file of the agent. In Codex, a command that sets CODEX_HOME in a way the guard does not see can point the check at transcripts that the agent wrote. A parent can tell a fresh agent to repeat a result that the parent wrote. When the parent changes the worktree while a fresh agent runs, its changes are in the output tree of that record. A commit that went around the gate has no trailer of the gate, so just ci stops it. The section “The trailer and just ci” tells how. A record that an agent wrote by hand gets through. The review of the pull request is the check of that. The scripts. .agents/skills/gcm/scripts/record_result.py writes the records. The hook record-result.sh runs it on SubagentStop. The recipes record and record-skip run it with uv, with pyyaml for the result block. The hook never stops the fresh agent. A result that gives no record only prints the reason.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: just has no log of its own. Its options --timestamp, --verbose and --explain print to the terminal, and its changelog shows that its internal logging was removed. So each Justfile sets jlog as its shell: set shell := ["jlog", "sh", "-cu"] jlog takes the real shell as its first argument, here sh -cu. It runs each line with that shell and the positional arguments of the recipe. Then it adds one JSON line to the run log: {"run": "48213-1731405600", "argv": ["just", "check"], "line": "uv run ruff check .", "exit": 0, "start": "2026-11-12T10:00:00Z", "end": "2026-11-12T10:00:04Z"} The run ID. The field run is JLOG_RUN when it is set. Without it, run is the process ID of the parent just and its start time, as in the example. The section “The steps” says where JLOG_RUN comes from. Where set shell goes. The installer writes the profiles as modules of just. A module has its own settings, so the installer writes set shell into each module file that it makes, and into .agents/install.just. It also writes it into the index file that the root Justfile imports. A setting in an imported file applies to the recipes of the root Justfile, as a test on 2026-11-12 showed. A repository that sets shell already. just stops with “Setting shell is redefined” when the root Justfile and an imported file both set it. So the installer looks for set shell in the root Justfile. When it finds one, it does not add its own. It asks the person to wrap the shell, for example ["jlog", "bash", "-c"]. The cost. Tests on 2026-11-12 on this machine measured the extra time for each line: Form of jlog Extra time for each line A POSIX shell script About 45 ms A Python script through uv About 100 ms A small compiled program About 1 to 2 ms, by estimate So jlog is a small compiled program, in a repository of its own. jagt stays a tool for agent packets only. No process for each line, other than the shell. jlog finds the log folder by going up from the current folder to the folder that holds .agents/, with no call to git. It computes no tree on each line. jlog has no code for a harness. It reads only the environment and the run log. Each harness has a plugin, and jlog calls the plugin once for each session. The run is the process ID of just and its start time. It joins the lines of one call. The argv is the just command as a list. jlog reads it from /proc/ /cmdline on Linux and with sysctl on macOS, which keeps the quoting. A skip comes from a jlog skip     line, not from the output of a tool. jlog does not read the output, so tools keep their terminal and colors. Backticks in a Justfile also run through jlog. It tags them as "kind": "backtick", and the gates ignore them. The log folder has its own .gitignore. On its first write, jlog makes .agents/log/.gitignore with the one line *. A test on 2026-11-12 showed that git add -A, git stash -u and git clean -fd then leave the folder alone. Without the file, git stash -u deleted the folder. jnterfaces also adds .agents/log/ to .gitignore, to .worktreedisposable and to its list of reserved folders. So a worktree with only a log folder can still be pruned. Secrets in lines. A line of a recipe can hold a secret, for example a value from a .env file or from an argument. jlog removes such values before it logs line and argv. It finds each variable that is not on the safe list and has a value of 8 characters or more. It replaces each such value with  . A request to just. A --log-file option in just itself would remove the need for jlog. Such a change is a request to the authors of just, outside this spec.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: jlog has commands of its own: Command What it logs jlog       One line of a recipe. just calls this form. jlog session The harness, the session ID, the path of the transcript and the model. jlog env The environment. jlog tools The version of each program in the tools table. jlog skip     A no-op step. jlog pass The pass of just check. Once for each session. The first line in a new session also runs session, env and tools. jlog marks a session as seen with a file .agents/log/sessions/ , so it reads no log to find out. jlog tools has a short timeout. The timeout is a few seconds. It starts no download, and its failure never fails the line. The gate is a plain script, not a recipe. So nothing runs on its own inside the git hook. The sandbox of Codex. In the mode workspace-write, Codex keeps .agents/ and .git/ read-only, also under a writable root of the folder above them. So just check cannot write its run log, the targets cannot write their packets, and git commit cannot write the git folder. The person approves these commands outside the sandbox. Or the person gives each of these folders as a sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots entry. The folders are .agents and .git of the main checkout, and in a worktree also its .agents and its git folder, from git rev-parse --git-dir. On 2026-11-16, with Codex 0.167.2, a codex exec commit in a main checkout checked the two roots of the main checkout. Probes with codex sandbox checked the four roots of a worktree. Which session. Each harness shows its session in a different way: Harness How jlog finds the session Source Codex Codex puts CODEX_THREAD_ID into each shell command that it runs. codex-rs/protocol/src/shell_environment.rs in openai/codex Claude Code CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is set in the shell commands. In a fresh agent, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION is set too, so jlog can tell the lines of a fresh agent from the lines of its parent. If the variable is missing, the SessionStart hook writes export JLOG_SESSION=... to the file in CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. The environment of a session on 2026-11-12, and the Claude Code hooks docs A person at a terminal The ID of the terminal session, from getsid(0). All just calls in one terminal then share one session. None The plugins. The repository of jlog has a folder plugins/, with one folder for each harness: plugins/ claude/ pyproject.toml uv.lock session.py codex/ pyproject.toml uv.lock session.py Each plugin is a uv project of its own. It has its own pyproject.toml, its own uv.lock and its own environment. So it does not depend on the Python of the system, or on the lock file of the repository in which jlog runs. jlog runs a plugin with uv run --project  /  --frozen python  / /session.py. The option --frozen uses the lock file as it is, and never changes it. A test on 2026-11-12 ran a plugin this way from the folder of another repository: The plugin used its own environment, in its own folder. The current folder stayed the folder of the repository. The repository did not change. After the first run, a call took about 40 ms. Where the plugins are. just install in the repository of jlog builds jlog and copies the plugins to ~/.local/share/jlog/plugins/. The variable JLOG_PLUGINS can name another folder. The plugins need no packages now. They use json from the standard library of Python. Their own lock files keep later packages away from other projects. A plugin reads only JSONL transcripts. It opens no database of a harness, because a read of a database in WAL mode writes to the folder of the harness. A new harness needs only a new folder in plugins/, and its hooks in agent_gest_git_skills. jlog and the gate do not change. Each plugin reads the environment and prints one JSON object: {"harness": "codex", "session": " ", "transcript": " ", "model": " ", "parent": " "} The environment. A recipe runs with sh, not with the shell of the person. A test on 2026-11-12 showed what a recipe gets: It gets the exported variables of the shell that ran just, for example PATH. It does not get aliases, shell functions, options, or variables that are set without export. It does not read .zshrc. A git hook gets the environment of the program that ran git. A GUI program or a CI runner does not read .zshrc. So these rules apply: A recipe never depends on .zshrc. The settings of a repository go in the Justfile, with set export, or in an ignored .env file, with set dotenv-load. The installer and the gate check that each program is on PATH. A missing program stops them with its install line. jlog env logs the names of all variables, and the values of a safe list only. The safe list has exact names, not prefixes. The names are PATH, SHELL, HOME, TERM, CI, CODEX_THREAD_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION. For any other variable, it logs the name and the word redacted. It also logs whether the value changed since the last session. It compares keyed hashes. The key stays on the machine, so a reader of the log cannot test a guess of the value. jlog session logs paths and IDs only. It never copies a transcript, because transcripts hold secrets.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The gates compare trees. An agent leaves its changes unstaged, so the trees come from the worktree, not from the index. The gate and the agentic targets compute the worktree tree as below, and jlog and jagt also start from a copy of the index: cp -p .git/index  /index # keeps the time of the index GIT_INDEX_FILE= /index git add -A GIT_INDEX_FILE= /index git write-tree The index file. GIT_INDEX_FILE names the index file that git uses. With a copy, the real index does not change. The copy keeps the time of the index, so git still checks the content of a file that changed in the same second as the index. The files of the index. A file that the index holds is in the tree, also when .gitignore names it. Other files that git ignores are not in the tree. Entries that git does not check. When an entry of the index is assume-unchanged or skip-worktree, the copy starts from HEAD with git read-tree HEAD instead. The object store. New objects go into a temporary object store. GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES names the real store, so git reads the old objects from it, and from the stores that the person already named there. Git splits that list at each :, so a path with :, " or \ goes in double quotes. No shared index. The setting core.splitIndex=false comes from the environment, so a split index leaves no new shared index file. At commit time, the commit tree must equal the worktree tree. So all changes must be staged: All changes staged. The commit tree equals the worktree tree, and the gates go on. Part of the changes staged. The commit stops. The gate prints the fix. Run git stash --keep-index -u, then the targets that the new tree needs and just check, then commit, then git stash pop.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The last line of check is jlog pass: check: fmt-check lint typecheck test integration coverage-check docstring-check docs-check prose-check diff-check jlog pass jlog computes the worktree tree at the first line of a run, and again at jlog pass. jlog pass writes a pass for the tree only if all of these hold: The nearest just above it in the process tree has the argv just check exactly, with no option and no NAME=VALUE. No variable of this list is set. The list is JUST_NO_DEPS, JUST_SHELL, JUST_JUSTFILE, JUST_WORKING_DIRECTORY, JUST_DOTENV_FILENAME and JUST_DOTENV_PATH. Other JUST_ variables, for example JUST_COLOR, do not matter. The log of this run has lines with exit 0 for each step in the list of .agents/stack.json. For a step that no profile provides, a skip also counts. The worktree tree at the end equals the worktree tree at the start. The worktree has no unstaged change and no untracked file that git does not ignore.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The gate is a plain script in agent_gest_git_skills. The git pre-commit hook runs it, because only that hook sees the real commit. git commit -a and git commit   each make the index after an agent hook runs. The gate does these checks: It checks that the steps and the required targets exist. It checks that the commit tree equals the worktree tree. It looks for a pass for the tree. It never runs the steps itself. A commit gives the hook a GIT_INDEX_FILE, and tests that run git can write into it and break the commit. If there is no pass, the gate stops and says “run just check”. For a commit by an agent, it looks for a chain of records that ends at the tree. It knows an agent by the variables of the harnesses, for example CODEX_THREAD_ID or CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. It stops the commit and says which target or step to run. The pre-merge-commit hook runs the same gate for git merge. The pre-commit framework. The tasker role installs the framework and owns .pre-commit-config.yaml. No profile installs it, so Python, TypeScript and Rust repositories have the same hooks. A project without the tasker role has no gate and no framework. The config has three local hooks: commit-gate runs the gate for the stages pre-commit and pre-merge-commit. commit-gate-trailer runs the gate again for the stage commit-msg, and adds the trailer Commit-Gate: to the message. just-ci runs just ci for the stage pre-push. So a push checks on your machine what CI checks, and a commit without a trailer stops before it reaches GitHub. The config also has the checks of pre-commit-hooks that change no file, such as check-yaml and detect-private-key, for a commit only. The config has no hook that changes files, such as ruff-format, trailing-whitespace or end-of-file-fixer. fmt-check and diff-check cover them. The role names two programs in install_extras.programs of its skill-package.json. The first is pre-commit itself, which uv tool install puts in the home folder. The second is the hooks. commit_gate.py --check-hooks checks the four hooks and the hooks of the config, and pre-commit install with a --hook-type for each of pre-commit, pre-merge-commit, commit-msg and pre-push installs them. jnterfaces installs the programs of a role after its files. The framework stashes the unstaged edits of tracked files before its hooks run. So the gate sees them as a tree without a pass, not as partial staging. The framework sets PRE_COMMIT=1 for its hooks, so then the stop also gives the stash fix. Untracked files stay in place, so they give the stop of partial staging. --check-hooks needs the hook commit-gate in the stages pre-commit and pre-merge-commit, so that git merge runs the gate too. The removal of the tasker role runs pre-commit uninstall for the four hooks, because a hook without its config stops each commit. The removal of a profile tool, such as lint, does not touch the hooks. When pre-commit cannot install. Outside a Git repository, the check of the hooks passes, and the first just install after git init installs them. With core.hooksPath set, as husky sets it, pre-commit refuses to install. The check then passes and prints the command of the gate, so that you can run the gate from the hooks of that folder. The required targets are in .agents/targets/required.txt. Each line names a target and the paths that make it required: review ** test-review @code update-docs @pages @api prose @pages @api The default. When the file is missing, the gate uses these lines. The syntax is that of git pathspecs with :(glob). So * does not match /, and ** does. A deleted path counts as a changed path. @api names the source files of the packages in packages. For a package pkg.sub, it is src/pkg/sub/** or pkg/sub/**, whichever exists, plus the check globs of the api settings. The api tool of each profile defines @api for its language. Only Python has one now. @pages names the files that is_page of nossaifd accepts. So AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md need no prose record. Without the nossaifd role, @pages is **/*.md and **/*.qmd. The gate reads is_page from .agents/skills/nossaifd/scripts/prose_gate.py in the parent commit, as it reads required.txt. So a change cannot loosen the rule for its own pages. The first commit has no parent, so the globs apply to it. The rule runs in a Python of its own. It gets the changed paths and gives back the pages. So it cannot end the gate or change its environment. The commit stops when the rule does not load, has no is_page, fails, ends before it checks each path, or gives back a path that the commit does not change. The message names the Python of the gate, because a rule can need a newer Python. @code names the source files of each language in .agents/stack.json. Each profile gives its globs under the key code of profile.json, for example **/*.py, **/*.ts or **/*.rs. The installer copies them into the key code of .agents/stack.json, for each profile. With no profile, @code is empty. Which file counts. The gate reads required.txt and .agents/generated.txt from the parent of the commit, so a commit cannot change the lists for itself. With no parent, or a parent without the file, the gate uses the default required.txt and an empty generated.txt. The steps come from the commit. jlog pass reads the steps of the worktree, so the gate reads them from the .agents/stack.json of the commit. A commit can then remove a tool and its step, and its review sees the change. @code takes both lists. It has the code globs of the commit and of the parent. So a commit that removes a language still needs test-review for its code. An amend replaces the last commit. The gate looks for --amend in the command line of git, with ps. A message can hold the same word, so the gate then applies the rules of both HEAD and its parent, and the stricter rules win. A bad line cannot land. The gate also reads the required.txt of the commit, and stops a line that it cannot read. A bad list in the parent, from before the gate, gives way to the default list. Which changes count. The gate compares the commit tree with the parent of the commit. Rules: Every commit needs a review record. A commit that changes code needs a test-review record. A commit with a docs file needs an update-docs record and a prose record. A commit that changes a module of the API pages needs the same two records. Its docstrings become text on the website. A change to other code needs neither record. The agent hooks of each harness do not check records. The gate guard, .agents/skills/gcm/scripts/gate_guard.py, parses the hook input as JSON and splits the command into words as a shell does, so a quoted message does not hide a flag. In Claude Code and in Codex, a PreToolUse hook that exits with 2 stops the command. The guard stops mistakes. It is not the lock, because a shell has too many ways to hide a command. The lock is the trailer of the gate. The hooks stop these plain commands: --no-verify, and -n with commit. core.hooksPath, git commit-tree and git update-ref. just record-skip, until the person agrees. In Claude Code the hook asks the person. In Codex it stops the command. A write to a log folder, .git/hooks, required.txt or the settings of the hooks. Other commands that make commits: Command Gate git commit The pre-commit hook. git merge The pre-merge-commit hook. git rebase, git cherry-pick, git revert Allowed. A lab checks which trees they make. The trailer and just ci. The gate stamps each commit that it passes, and CI checks the stamps: The trailer. The commit-msg hook runs the gate once more. Then it adds Commit-Gate: patch:  to the message. A merge gets Commit-Gate: tree: . The patch ID is the hash of the change, from git patch-id --verbatim, which keeps the spaces of each line. The diff has no lines of context, so a rebase with no conflict keeps the ID, and a restacked branch still passes. An added line that moves within one part of a file keeps the ID too. The trailer is a claim, so that cost is fair. A file of git add -N is not in the ID, since the commit does not hold it. An amend. For what looks like an amend, the trailer names the patch IDs against both possible parents. When HEAD is a merge, it names the tree too, since the amend is a merge. A skip shows. git commit -n skips the commit-msg hook too. So a commit that went around the gate has no trailer. just ci runs ci-gate, then the steps in the list ci of .agents/stack.json. jnterfaces writes the recipe ci, and the tasker role gives ci-gate. Without the role, ci-gate only says that there is no gate. ci-gate runs commit_gate.py --trailers on each commit of a range. Each commit needs a trailer that names its own patch ID, or its own tree for a merge. The range comes from the first of these that is there: JN_CI_BASE and JN_CI_HEAD, which CI sets. PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF and PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF, which the pre-push hook sets for a push to a branch that the remote has. PRE_COMMIT_LOCAL_BRANCH alone, for a push of a new history. Each commit of the branch counts. By hand, the upstream of the branch, or else origin/HEAD. With neither, ci-gate fails and says to set JN_CI_BASE. Limits of the pre-push hook. The framework reads only the first branch of a push. So git push origin a b checks the commits of a. CI checks each pull request. A push to a new, empty remote checks each commit of the branch. A repository with commits from before the gate needs git push --no-verify for that push. Commits that git makes without the hooks. git revert --no-edit runs no commit-msg hook, and a squash of git rebase --autosquash keeps the old trailer. Each one stops the push until git commit --amend --no-edit gives it a new trailer. CI is a part of just check. A step in the list ci must be a step of just check. The installer leaves out any other name and says so. The default list is empty. Put a step in it only when a clean machine tells you more than your own machine, for example a test on Linux. No agent runs in CI. The fresh agents run before each commit, on the machine of the person. CI reads only their trailers. The limit. A trailer is a claim of the gate, not a proof. An agent can type one by hand. The review of the pull request is the check of that. The cost. The agent runs just check before it commits, and the gate only reads the pass. Integration tests stay in just check by default, so a slow suite makes each commit slow. The setup question integration can move them to just verify, which runs before a PR.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The spec drops GitButler, so a stack of dependent PRs uses plain git: Each branch starts from the branch below it. gh pr create --base   opens the PR of each branch. git rebase --update-refs moves the branches of a stack together after a change to a lower branch. Git 2.38 and later have it. A recipe of the tasker role opens the PRs of a stack in order, from the bottom branch up.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
text: The trigger is the CI workflow of the docs tool, on a push to main. It runs just docs-publish. The workflow has permissions: contents: write and sets GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}, so gh and the push to gh-pages work. The GitHub Pages source needs one setting by a person, once. The visibility check. just docs-publish asks gh repo view --json visibility. It publishes with smalldocs only on PUBLIC. On PRIVATE and on INTERNAL, it logs a skip. Errors. On a machine of a person, an error of gh logs a skip, so a failure never publishes. In CI, where CI=true, an error of gh fails the job, so a missing token shows as a failure.

title: Spec: Commit gates for any repository
section: The files that the installer writes
text: The installer of jnterfaces already composes shared files. Each owner declares its lines and its parts. The installer keeps one block for each owner, and an uninstall removes only that block. scripts/formats.json says how to read and write each shared file. The spec uses this writer for each file that it adds to: File Owner Piece .gitignore jnterfaces The line .agents/log/. .worktreedisposable jnterfaces The line .agents/log/. .gitignore Each profile The paths of its caches and coverage reports. .agents/generated.txt, .agents/coverage-exclude.txt jnterfaces writes them empty, once, in a project that it started The person or the agent adds paths, and creates the file when it is missing. test-review judges each one. A project with a Justfile of its own gets neither file, and a missing list counts as empty. .pre-commit-config.yaml The tasker role The local hooks of the gate and of just ci, and the checks of pre-commit-hooks that change no file. So a local entry of the project takes the place of the entry of the role, and commit_gate.py --check-hooks fails and says to copy the hooks of the role into it. .claude/settings.json The tasker role The hooks SessionStart, SubagentStop and PreToolUse. The hooks of GitButler go: Stop with gitbutler-snapshot.sh, and gitbutler-vcs-context.sh. .codex/hooks.json The tasker role The hooks SessionStart, SubagentStop and PreToolUse. The GitButler hooks and text go. .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json The nossaifd role The turn gate of nossaifd, UserPromptSubmit and Stop, as now. The smalldocs config The docs tool and the api tool The site settings, and the api settings. formats.json needs a new entry for this file. The nossaifd role also writes .github/workflows/nossaifd-prose.yml, as a seed and as a starter. Each is a whole file, not a piece. When the tasker role is installed, just check in CI runs prose-check. So the installer removes that file, whichever entry wrote it, and does not write it again while the tasker role is installed. The tasker role writes the CI job, .github/workflows/check.yml, as a starter only. It is a whole file, and it is yours from then on. An older installer takes a seed out on removal, so the job has no seed. The tasker role ships it only after jnterfaces writes the check recipe: The events. It runs on each pull request. It does not use pull_request_target, which would give the code of the pull request the secrets of the repository. The history. The checkout has fetch-depth: 0, so ci-gate can read each commit. It checks out the head of the pull request. The merge commit that GitHub makes has no trailer. The tools. It installs just, uv, and jlog at a tagged release. The person adds the setup of the tools of a language that the runner lacks. The run. It runs just ci on the committed files, and not just install. An install can change tracked files. It gives ci-gate the base of the pull request in JN_CI_BASE. The run log, the packets and the records are not pieces. The runs write them, in the log folders.
